Question 1
?

A particle moves from the origin with an acceleration of (2i−4j)in/s2 and an initial velocity of (i−2j)in/s. Find the position vector of the particle after 3 seconds.

a
(12i+3j)in
b
(12i−24j)in
c
(−3i+14j)in
d
(−6i−7j)in
e
(8i+9j)in
Submit

decision.explanation: With constant acceleration, r(t)=r(0)+v(0)t+½at². Thus r(3)=3(i−2j)+(9/2)(2i−4j)=(12i−24j) in.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: A particle moves from the origin with an acceleration of $(2i-4j)\,{\text{in/s}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $(i-2j)\,\text{in/s}.$ Find the position vector of the particle after $3$ seconds.
after.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $a,$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut+\frac{1}{2}a{t}^{2},
$$

 

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle and $u$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=0i+0j,\,u=i-2j,\,a=2i-4j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t=3\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(0i+0j)+(i-2j)(3)+\frac{1}{2}(2i-4j)(3)^{2} \\  & =(3i-6j)+9(i-2j) \\  & =(3i-6j)+(9i-18j) \\  & =(12i-24j)\,\text{in}.\end{aligned}
$$

If a particle moves with constant acceleration a, the position vector of the particle at time t can be found using

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: A particle moves from the origin with an acceleration of $(-2i+j)\,{\text{ft/s}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $(4i+j)\,\text{ft/s}.$ Find the distance from the particle to the origin after $4$ seconds.
after.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $a,$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut+\frac{1}{2}a{t}^{2},
$$

 

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle and $u$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=0i+0j,\,u=4i+j,\,a=-2i+j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t=4\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(0i+0j)+(4i+j)(4)+\frac{1}{2}(-2i+j)(4)^{2} \\  & =(16i+4j)+8(-2i+j) \\  & =(16i+4j)+(-16i+8j) \\  & =12j\,\text{ft}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance from the particle to the origin at this time is

$$
\begin{aligned}|r| & =|12j| \\  & =|12| \\  & =12\,\text{ft}.\end{aligned}
$$
